changes: Fewer invented lines: the speech recognition likes to "hear" "Thank you." or "Tschüss" in music or silence. These are now dropped when the recognition itself is unsure about them. On 25 test videos this removed about a fifth of all invented lines.

Better speaker detection in long videos with many characters: short snippets no longer pile up into extra "characters" that mix several voices. In a test episode with 10 characters, Voicitool now finds exactly 10 instead of 17.

New Voicitool.exe: Windows Defender wrongly flagged the previous one as "Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml". The new exe drops a start option that virus scanners often dislike and has been reported to Microsoft as a false alarm.
Faster speech recognition on PCs without an NVIDIA graphics card: it now uses all processor cores instead of four.
The setup now always installs the x64 version of Python, so it should also work on Windows laptops with an ARM processor (for example Snapdragon). Not tested on such a laptop yet.
Voicitool now reports once a day that it is in use (only "active" and the build number), so I can see roughly how many people use it. You can switch this off under Settings, Updates.
Voicitool and the setup now start in your Windows language. The setup language can be changed at the top right.
Updates can be installed from inside the app: a note appears at the top when a new version is out.
After starting, the small start window stays until Voicitool is ready and then brings it to the front.
After an update, the installation is checked in the background instead of opening the whole setup.
A failed update no longer blocks the start. Voicitool then simply starts the version you already have.
